card.name: Overdose and emergency treatment wording
card.fires_on: Small words or word parts in overdose and emergency-treatment sentences, just before urgent-action wording such as 'of first importance', 'prompt', or 'to treat anaphylaxis'.

modes.label: Cardiovascular support line
modes.description: The word 'is' after 'support of the cardiovascular system' in overdosage text on low blood pressure.
modes.example: support of the cardiovascular system<< is>> of first importance. Restoration of blood pressure

modes.label: Linking word before urgent treatment
modes.description: The word 'to' or a comma that leads into emergency treatment, such as treating anaphylaxis or hemodialysis.
modes.example: and medications<< to>> treat anaphylaxis are readily available

modes.label: Inside drug names in emergency text
modes.description: Partway through a drug name such as epinephrine or pyridostigmine in antidote and rescue-treatment sentences.
modes.example: discontinue pyrid<<ost>>igmine bromide and administer pretreatment

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward words about speed and urgency, such as rapid and prompt, and away from words about routine or recurring events.
card.plain: It fires in overdose and emergency passages where the text is about to say that treatment must be quick.
